stage1.impression: A red-and-white milk-carton speaker in a sunlit, minimal room: the product reads at once and the low sun throwing its silhouette on the wall is a good story, but the white front is a flat, near-clipped slab, the floor contact looks weak and the wall shadow seems to float detached from the speaker. The set (plain plank floor, stool-like table with a twig vase, a lot of blank wall) reads as stock CG with some smearing, and the product is small in a frame that is mostly empty wall.

blocking_9: The white front carries a smooth sheen of at least 5 levels from eave to mid-face with no channel at 254; now it is one value, 243.4 to 241.9 down the clean strip [504,332,512,655] (falloff 1.5), so the lacquer reads as card.

All seven letters of the wordmark evenly lit and legible: letter p5 >= 150 and under 3% of letter pixels clipped; now p5 99, p95 253, 39.7% clipped, with r-m-i fused into one white blob (252, blue 255) between a dull e (129) and k (133).
The white body reads white in shade: the side within dE2000 3 of a neutral grey of its lightness; now [183,172,168], R-B +15, dE2000 5.29 vs #ACACAC.

Shade is neutral to cool against warm sun: the speaker's wall shadow within dE2000 4.5 of neutral; now [186,171,164], hue 53 deg, chroma 7.0, dE2000 7.26 vs #B4B4B4, pinker and more chromatic than the sun patch (hue 75 deg, chroma 5.6).
A bright, airy key: the unlit back wall median >= 206 (now 199.5 on [300,20,1300,200], 190.8 under the ceiling) while the sun patch stays >= 25 levels above it and the front white <= 247.
The floor reads as oak, not laminate: >= 14 levels of plank-to-plank variation in an evenly lit patch (now lum_range 9.7 on [0,740,330,800]; neighbouring planks differ by 2 to 8 levels).
The props look art-directed: the side table is a square-legged stool in the floor's own honey tone (leg median 108, top 121 against floor about 142), so it reads as a default asset.

changes.problem: The wordmark's 6 cm glint lamp covers only the middle letters, so r-m-i blow out into one white blob while e and k stay dull grey and the brand name does not read.

evidence.measured: part letters-front-*: median per letter e 129, a 233, r 252, m 252, i 248, l 198, k 133 (r, m, i at blue 255); x-profile across the word 130, 178, 252, 252, 252, 209, 131; p5 99.1, p95 252.9, clip_pct 39.7

changes.expected: One broad, soft highlight across all seven letters at the same power (about 11x lower radiance per area): letter medians within about 170-230, none clipped (letter clip_pct under 3), letter p5 from 99 to 150-215; the cast letters read as one satin-metal wordmark.

changes.problem: The white lacquered front is a single value from eave to plinth, so it reads as a paper card: its clear coat mirrors only the dim floor and lower left wall (mirror ray to azimuth -55 deg, 9 deg downward) and the sunlit white sits in the view transform's shoulder.

evidence.measured: clean white strip between woofer and front/side corner: profile 243.4, 243.5, 243.5, 243.5, 242.8, 242.7, 241.9, 241.9 (falloff 1.5, p5-p95 241.1-243.8); left strip [391,330,398,630] 244.4 to 242.8; the whole white front (front-baffle in [389,325,520,650]) median 243.6, clip 0

changes.expected: A sky sheen in the lacquer, brightest under the eave and gone by mid-face: on the strip the top bin rises to 247-250 while the bottom bins stay about 242 (falloff 5-8), the left strip shows the same ramp, and no front pixel reaches 254. The panel sits 0.8 m out along the front's mirror ray and is kept clear of the sunbeam that lights the front; being reflection-only it must cast no shadow anywhere in the frame.

changes.problem: The white body's shaded side reads beige-pink rather than white in shade, because the neutral fill is outweighed by warm bounce from the honey floor and the sunlit wall.

evidence.measured: side-right within this box: rgb median [183, 172, 168] (R-B +15; Lab a +3.2, b +3.5), dE2000 5.29 vs neutral #ACACAC of the same lightness, luminance median 173.8; the plinth's shaded red [530,665,600,690] has drifted orange to [141, 24, 9] (dE2000 4.6 vs the spec hue at that lightness, #8D1C1C)

changes.expected: A cool, sky-like fill cancels the pink-orange bounce: the side within dE2000 3 of neutral, R-B within +/-5, luminance median still 165-180; the plinth side's blue channel rises from 9 toward its green, back toward the spec red's hue.

changes.problem: The room's shade is pinker and more chromatic than its sunlight, which inverts the warm-sun, cool-shade contrast that makes light read as morning sun.

evidence.measured: the speaker's shadow on the wall: rgb [186, 171, 164], Lab a +4.2 b +5.5 (hue 53 deg, chroma 7.0), dE2000 7.05 vs #AEAEAE and 7.26 vs #B4B4B4; the sun patch [950,380,1100,520] is [246, 237, 228], hue 75 deg, chroma 5.6; the unlit wall beside the speaker [340,330,385,500] is [210, 206, 209], a magenta grey

changes.expected: The skylight through the windows takes a cool, slightly cyan cast at nearly the same luminance (Y 0.80 vs 0.83) and pulls the shade toward neutral: the wall shadow's R-B from +22 to <= +8 and within dE2000 4.5 of neutral grey, while the sun patch stays cream (R-B >= +12) because the sun dominates it.

changes.problem: The unlit back wall is a dull mid-light grey, so the room reads dim rather than bright and airy; exposure cannot lift it because the sunlit white front already sits at 243.6 in the shoulder, so the shade has to come up through the sky.

evidence.measured: upper wall median 199.5 (p5 192.7, p95 207.2), 190.8 just under the ceiling ([600,0,900,30]); sun patch 238.3; front white 243.6

changes.expected: The shade lifts more than the sunlight: upper wall median 206-214, sun patch about 240 and still >= 25 above the wall, the speaker's wall shadow about 180 (the silhouette still >= 55 below the patch), front white <= 246.

changes.problem: The oak floor reads as printed laminate: neighbouring planks differ by only 2 to 8 levels and the grain does not show at this scale.

evidence.measured: evenly lit floor patch: lum_range 9.7 (p5 141.1, p95 150.8), profile flat at 145-148; foreground column [1180,720,1200,900] plank steps 149.8 to 141.8 to 134.6, the largest 8 levels

changes.expected: Visible plank-to-plank variation of about 6-14 levels without striping; the patch's lum_range 14-24 with its median unchanged at about 145.

out_of_scope.request: Widen the 3 mm shadow lines under the gable and over the plinth (or deepen them into a visible dark groove) so the gable, body and plinth read as assembled parts.
out_of_scope.why: At this frame's roughly 0.34 px/mm they render sub-pixel: the gable-to-white junction steps red 80 -> 191 -> 242 and the white-to-plinth junction 241 -> 168 -> 70 with no dark line, so the carton reads as one moulded block and loses its cabinet-maker detail; the lines are spec geometry, and the sun cannot be raised to shade them without dropping the speaker out of the window's beam.
